ads_ratio.reason: 20-F filer: EDGAR per-share figures are per ordinary share while the Nasdaq price ($15.51) is per ADS; engine per-share figures must be scaled by the 10:1 ADS ratio to be comparable to the traded price.
ads_ratio.source: Vodafone Group Plc Form 20-F (filed 14 June 2024), cover page: American Depositary Shares 'each representing ten ordinary shares'; same ratio stated in the depositary (BNY) ADR records for CUSIP 92857W209

moat_against: Commodity connectivity: low switching costs, MVNO and price competition, esp. Germany
Regulated returns: spectrum auctions, wholesale-access mandates, price interventions cap ROCE (below WACC for years)
Structural decline in legacy fixed/voice; OTT players capture the value layer above the network
Emerging-market/FX exposure: Turkiye hyperinflation accounting, EGP/ZAR volatility
Leverage constrains the investment race: net debt EUR 25.4B at FY26-end plus GBP 4.3B cash buyout of CK Hutchison's 49% of VodafoneThree
moat_for: Scarce licensed spectrum + sunk network assets in 15+ markets
VodafoneThree: UK's largest mobile operator (~28m customers), GBP 1bn/yr synergy target by FY32
Germany scale: largest single market, cable/fibre footprint to ~75% of homes
Vodacom + M-Pesa: African growth and mobile-money franchise (Safaricom stake raised to 55%)
Vodafone Business: global enterprise, IoT platform (240m+ connections), digital services growing high-double-digit
moat_justification: Weak moat (4/10). Vodafone owns scarce spectrum and sunk network infrastructure in 15+ markets and is now the UK's largest mobile operator via VodafoneThree, with real scale in Germany (largest market), a majority stake in Vodacom with M-Pesa financial services in Africa, and a top-tier enterprise/IoT franchise. But connectivity is a commodity: switching costs are low, regulators cap returns and mandate wholesale access, MVNOs and price competition (Germany especially) grind ARPU, and ROCE has run below the cost of capital for years — the FY26 investor targets only promise ROCE above WACC by FY32. Scale buys survival and synergies, not pricing power.
name: Vodafone Group Plc
one_liner: Post-restructuring telecom, moat 4/10 — engine prints Tier S (32.6% weighted IRR, IV@15 $37.13) only because its capex tag misses spectrum/intangible capex, lease principal and cash interest; on Vodafone's own adjusted FCF (EUR 2.6B in FY26) the cash yield is ~7% with low-single-digit guided growth, so it does not clear 15% at $15.51 — final tier D by override, numbers tier S retained.
tier_override_reason: Model-measurement artifact: the engine's conservative OE subtracts capex only from the PP&E-purchase tag (EUR ~4.3B FY25) off OCF as filed, so it excludes the cash costs that dominate telecom economics — spectrum and intangible capital additions (group capital additions were EUR 6.9B in FY25 per the FY26 results presentation), lease principal payments, and cash interest. Vodafone's own adjusted free cash flow was EUR 2.5B in FY25 vs the engine's EUR 10.9B OE total for the same year. Every scenario inherits the inflated base, so even the super-bear IRR (17.6%) is an artifact. On the company's own cash measure the ADS yields roughly 7% with low-single-digit guided FCF growth — a D-tier return profile at $15.51. Tier set to D; tier_by_numbers (S) retained in score.json.
